meta.description: Practical endgame guidance - decision making, transitions, common scenarios

sections.name: Middlegame to Endgame Transition Decisions
sections.description: When to trade, what to keep, how to evaluate resulting endings

principles.action: Trade pieces, not pawns. Simplify to winning endgame.
principles.exceptions: Attack against king > material; initiative worth more than pawn

principles.action: Avoid trades, create complications, seek perpetual/stalemate
principles.exceptions: Trade into drawn theoretical ending (opposite bishops, Philidor)

principles.action: Trade pieces to highlight structural advantage
principles.exceptions: Need pieces to attack weaknesses; king not safe

principles.action: Avoid piece trades, seek counterplay, complicate
principles.exceptions: Trade into opposite-color bishops or known fortress

checklist: Identify theoretical ending result if traded

sections.name: Which Pieces to Trade/Keep
sections.description: Specific guidance for each piece type

tradeWhen: Opponent's rook more active (on 7th, open file)
keepWhen: Need rook for passed pawn support

tradeWhen: Your bishop is bad (blocked by own pawns)
Opponent has good bishop, you have knight
keepWhen: Endgame with pawns on both wings

tradeWhen: Closed position, knight has no outpost
Entering pawn ending where knight bad

guidelines.notes: King activation is THE key endgame principle. Centralize early.

sections.name: Common Practical Scenarios
sections.description: Frequently occurring positions with practical guidance

guidance.attacker: Aim for Lucena: rook behind pawn, king in front, build bridge
guidance.defender: Aim for Philidor: rook on 6th rank, king in front, check from behind
guidance.key: Rook behind passer = win; rook on 6th = draw

guidance.attacker: Fix pawns on YOUR bishop's color, attack on opposite color, centralize king
guidance.defender: Fix pawns on OPPONENT's bishop color, create fortress, king active
guidance.key: Often drawn even 2 pawns down; don't overpress

aggressionMod.41-60: Try to win if extra pawn

guidance.bishopSide: Open position, pawns on both wings, fix pawns on opposite color to bishop
guidance.knightSide: Closed position, create outpost, fix pawns on bishop's color

scenarios.name: Queen vs Rook + Pawn (or Queen + Pawn vs Queen)

guidance.queenSide: Centralize queen, avoid perpetual, king approaches, watch stalemate
guidance.rookSide: Rook + king shelter, perpetual check, pawn promotion threats
guidance.key: Queen usually wins but perpetual danger high

scenarios.name: King and Pawn Race (Both sides passed pawns)

guidance.both: Calculate precisely! Who promotes first? Who promotes with check? Queen vs Queen endgame?
guidance.key: Count moves exactly; queen with check often wins

guidance.attacker: Keep rook on 7th, create mating threats, win pawns, don't trade rook!
guidance.defender: Trade rooks if possible, create counterplay, activate king
guidance.key: Rook on 7th often worth a pawn; activity principle

sections.name: Endgame Time Management
principles: Endgames require MORE time per move, not less
In theoretical positions (Lucena, Philidor): play instantly if known
In complex positions: use time to calculate, not to 'think'
Flagging risk: simplify if low on time, complicate if opponent low
Increment: use it! Don't play instant moves in critical positions

clockScenarios.moderateTime: Focus on key decisions (trade or not, which piece), verify calculations
clockScenarios.lowTime: Simplify to known positions, avoid complex calculations, premove obvious
clockScenarios.criticalTime: Pre-move forced sequences, simplify maximally, flagging tactics

sections.name: Psychological Factors in Endgames
principles: Endgames are not 'boring' - they're pure chess
Fatigue sets in: stay hydrated, breathe, stand up between moves
Opponent may relax in 'drawn' endings - stay alert
Convert winning positions: technique over creativity
Defend difficult positions: active defense, create problems
Don't offer draws in winning positions (unless tournament situation)
Respect opponent's time trouble - don't blunder trying to flag

0-20.philosophy: Technique over tricks. Convert advantages methodically.
0-20.tradePolicy: Trade pieces aggressively into known wins
0-20.riskTolerance: Zero. Only play theoretically won endings.

21-40.tradePolicy: Trade into favorable endings, keep pieces if attack exists

41-60.philosophy: Flexible. Win if winning, draw if not, complicate if losing.
41-60.tradePolicy: Case by case. Activity often > material.

61-80.philosophy: Keep pieces, create chaos, avoid theoretical endings.
61-80.tradePolicy: Avoid trades. Keep tension. Rook on 7th > pawn.

81-100.philosophy: Endgame? What endgame? Mate or flag.
81-100.tradePolicy: Never trade. King walks. Perpetual check.
